title: Lower bounds and classical counit comparison for exact derived adjoints
statement:
Let $\mathcal A_Z,\mathcal A_X,\mathcal B_Z,\mathcal B_X$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and their standard t-structures [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Write $D^+$ for cohomology bounded below. Let $F:D(\mathcal A_Z)\to D(\mathcal A_X)$ preserve $D^{\le m}$ and $D^{\ge m}$ for every integer $m$. Fix adjunctions $F\dashv G$ and $F\dashv J$, with counits $\epsilon^G$ and $\epsilon^J$, and let $\gamma:G\xrightarrow{\sim}J$ be their counit-normalized isomorphism [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], so $\epsilon^J_N\circ F(\gamma_N)=\epsilon^G_N$.

Let $S_T:D(\mathcal A_T)\to D(\mathcal B_T)$, for $T=X,Z$, be functors preserving cohomological lower bounds. Suppose $S_X$ has a right adjoint $U_X$, with unit $\eta$ and counit $e$, and $\eta_N:N\to U_XS_XN$ is invertible for all $N\in D^+(\mathcal A_X)$. Let $P:D(\mathcal B_Z)\to D(\mathcal B_X)$ be a functor and fix a natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_H:S_XFH\xrightarrow{\sim}PS_ZH\qquad(H\in D^+(\mathcal A_Z)).$$
Here the displayed adjunctions include their unit and counit triangle identities; all naturality assertions refer to the given functors and adjunctions.

For every integer $a$ and $N\in D^{\ge a}(\mathcal A_X)$, both $JN$ and $GN$ lie in $D^{\ge a}(\mathcal A_Z)$. For $N\in D^+(\mathcal A_X)$ put
$$K_N=S_XN,\qquad D_N=JN,\qquad E_N=GU_XS_XN,\qquad r_N=\eta_N^{-1}.$$
Then $D_N,E_N$ are bounded below, and the natural maps
$$\beta_N=\gamma_N\circ G(r_N):E_N\xrightarrow{\sim}D_N,\qquad\alpha_N=S_Z(\beta_N):S_ZE_N\xrightarrow{\sim}S_ZD_N$$
are isomorphisms. Define the morphism
$$t_N=e_{K_N}\circ S_X(\epsilon^G_{U_XK_N})\circ\lambda_{E_N}^{-1}:PS_ZE_N\longrightarrow K_N.$$
It satisfies the counit comparison equation
$$t_N=S_X(\epsilon^J_N)\circ\lambda_{D_N}^{-1}\circ P(\alpha_N).$$
All these isomorphisms and equations are natural in $N\in D^+(\mathcal A_X)$. No assertion that $P$ has an ambient right adjoint is made.

proof.text: Fix $a$ and $N\in D^{\ge a}(\mathcal A_X)$. For every $A\in D^{\le a-1}(\mathcal A_Z)$, the hypothesis on $F$ gives $FA\in D^{\le a-1}(\mathcal A_X)$. By [lem-pc-derived-tstructure-orthogonality], $\operatorname{Hom}(FA,N)$ has only its zero morphism. The given adjunction bijections identify this singleton with each of $\operatorname{Hom}(A,GN)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(A,JN)$. Each latter set therefore also consists only of its zero morphism. Apply [lem-pur-tstructure-lower-bound-hom-test] in the standard t-structure to obtain $GN,JN\in D^{\ge a}$. This singleton argument needs no unstated additivity assumption on $F$.

source.place: 1.3.4, p. 30, right orthogonal characterization; agent application to the supplied adjunctions

proof.text: For $N\in D^+$ choose $a$ with $N\in D^{\ge a}$. Step 1 gives $D_N=JN\in D^{\ge a}$. The supplied isomorphism $\eta_N:N\xrightarrow{\sim}U_XS_XN$ puts $U_XS_XN$ in the same strictly full subcategory $D^{\ge a}$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], so Step 1 gives $E_N=GU_XS_XN\in D^{\ge a}$. Thus both inputs of $\lambda$ used below belong to its prescribed domain. Since $r_N$ and $\gamma_N$ are isomorphisms, functors preserve their inverses and hence $\beta_N=\gamma_N\circ G(r_N)$ and $\alpha_N=S_Z(\beta_N)$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and the following unit/counit formulas; elementary calculation for the supplied adjunctions

proof.text: The triangle identity for $S_X\dashv U_X$ at $N$ is $e_{S_XN}\circ S_X(\eta_N)=1_{S_XN}$. Since $\eta_N$ is invertible, compose on the right with $S_X(r_N)$ to obtain $e_{K_N}=S_X(r_N)$. This uses the actual given unit, not an arbitrary isomorphism $N\cong U_XS_XN$.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and the following unit/counit formulas; elementary calculation for the supplied adjunctions

proof.text: Counit naturality for $F\dashv G$ at $r_N:U_XK_N\to N$ gives $r_N\circ\epsilon^G_{U_XK_N}=\epsilon^G_N\circ F(G(r_N))$. The normalization from [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] gives $\epsilon^G_N=\epsilon^J_N\circ F(\gamma_N)$. Substitute Step 3 and these identities in the definition of $t_N$ and use functoriality to get $$t_N=S_X(\epsilon^J_N)\circ S_XF(\beta_N)\circ\lambda_{E_N}^{-1}.$$

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and the following unit/counit formulas; elementary calculation for the supplied adjunctions

proof.text: Naturality of the given $\lambda$ at $\beta_N:E_N\to D_N$ gives $P S_Z(\beta_N)\circ\lambda_{E_N}=\lambda_{D_N}\circ S_XF(\beta_N)$. Composing with both inverses yields $S_XF(\beta_N)\circ\lambda_{E_N}^{-1}=\lambda_{D_N}^{-1}\circ P(\alpha_N)$. Substitute into Step 4 to obtain the required equation.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and the following unit/counit formulas; elementary calculation for the supplied adjunctions

proof.text: For a morphism $h:N\to N'$ in $D^+$, naturality of $\eta$ gives $r_{N'}\circ U_XS_X(h)=h\circ r_N$ by multiplication with its inverse components. Naturality of the given $\gamma$ then gives $J(h)\circ\beta_N=\beta_{N'}\circ GU_XS_X(h)$. Applying $S_Z$ proves naturality of $\alpha$. The definition of $t$ is a composite of natural transformations: the restrictions of $e$, $S_X\epsilon^G$, and $\lambda^{-1}$ along the indicated functors. These restrictions are defined because Step 2 puts $E_N$ in $D^+$ for every $N$ in the domain. Thus $t$ is natural. The right side of Step 5 is likewise a composite of $S_X\epsilon^J$, $\lambda^{-1}$ and $P\alpha$, proving all the asserted naturality.
